To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have designed, synthesized and evaluated a series of D-gluta-mic acid based inhibitors of MurD ligase incorporating the 5- benzylidenethiazol-din-4-one moiety.
we designed, synthesized, evaluated, and characterized a new series of potent MurD inhibitors incorporating a 5-benzoylidenethiazolidine scaffold.

the crystal structures of the MurD active sites in complex with inhibitors 16 and 18 have provided a good starting platform for the design of new inhibitors incorporating the 1-benzylidenetetrahydrothiopyran-2-one scaffold and that compounds 73-75 have shown improved MurD inhibiting potency (IC( 50) between 2.9 and 6.8 μM) and represent the most potent inhibitors reported to date.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the discovery of a new MurD ligase inhibitor class and provides a good starting point to design new MurD inhibitors endowed with improved antibacterial activity.
the identification of novel MurD inhibitors and with the development of a new series with a novel scaffold.
the identification of new MurD inhibitors that could be useful in the development of novel anti-infectives.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
MurD inhibitors based on the 5-benzenidenethiazolidine-4-one scaffold have a promising potential as antibacterial drugs.
the D-Glu scaffold is a viable MurD inhibitor scaffold, which can be further developed into a lead compound for the development of new antibacterial agents.
the D-glutamate moiety can be successfully replaced by 5-benzilidenethiazolidine-4-one, a structural feature present in several clinically relevant β-lactam antibiotics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
MurD inhibitors based on the D-glutamate template are not as potent as MurD inhibitors based upon the D-alanine template.

the design of novel inhibitors based on the 5-benzyldienethiazolidinone scaffold has been successful in the case of the D-glutamic-based MurD inhibitors, whereas it has not been so in the case of MurA inhibitors.
the design of novel MurD ligase inhibitors is a viable strategy in the search for new antibacterial drugs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 5-benzenidenethiazolidine scaffold is a viable alternative to the 4-benzylideneimidazolidin-2-one scaffold, which has been widely used in MurD inhibitors.

MurD inhibition can be achieved using D-Glu-based inhibitors and that the MurD active-site structure can be successfully exploited to guide the rational design of new inhibitors with improved potency.
the 5-benzyldienethiazolidinone scaffold, previously used in the design of MurA and MurC inhibitors, can also be used as a starting scaffold for the development of novel MurD inhibitors.
